title: Freetown: roads, floods and losses
about: Freetown's centre and east, within 4.5 km (World Bank, JBA Risk Management and Freetown City Council's Flood Risk Assessment, CC BY 4.0; Overture Maps; GHS-POP). The plan ranks the road links by what the river floods at six return periods cost through each and by what losing each would add; reads coverage by the buildings mapped as care in each flood and where three more would reach most; brings the people of the 1-in-100-year river flood out to dry ground, all at once and leaving as people did in Miyako in 2011 (the survey's shares, declared here); prices what the floods would cost its 153,435 buildings under every model of the JRC's global depth–damage curves for three regions, as a range; and meets the city's 1,943 modelled flood events with layers of a budget, a credit and insurance. Every speed and cost is declared.
